title: Ingress Arbiter: runtime schema adjudication and soft-coercion service for usage events
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Our current usage-event ingestion pipeline rejects or misclassifies a small but growing slice (~0.6%) of payloads when upstream SDKs or third-party integrations mutate shapes (new optional fields, minor type changes, enum variants). These rejections show up as customer noise and backfill work for platform engineers.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, low-latency service (Ingress Arbiter) that sits between the edge ingestion tier and the canonical event router to make deterministic, explainable decisions about partially incompatible payloads. The Arbiter will: (1) apply layered schema checks (strict -> permissive -> fuzzy), (2) score violations and decide accept/reject/coerce based on policy + historical scoreboard, (3) emit rich telemetry and explainability metadata for downstream consumers and audits, and (4) expose a rollout control plane for canarying and automatic fallback.

Non-goals: This ticket is not changing long-term storage schemas or end-user schema contracts. It is explicitly for admission-time decisions and observability only. Full data migration/backfill will be separate work.

High-level approach and components:
- Validation pipeline: JSON Schema + typed shape checks -> type-casting heuristics (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers when safe) -> fuzzy enum mapping (Levenshtein / canonicalization table) -> semantic accept with provenance metadata.
- Scoring engine: generate a deterministic score for each payload (0.0..1.0) representing confidence. Policies map score ranges to actions: accept-as-is, accept-with-coercion, route-to-quarantine, reject.
- Policy store: per-tenant and global policies, stored in Console config service (with feature flags).
- Observability: emit structured events for every adjudication decision with fields: score, rule_hit_list, pre/post shape diff, applied_coercions, policy_id, sample_id. Hook into Console dashboards and alerts 
- Performance budget: <2ms median additional latency at the ingress tier for validated requests, 99th percentile <8ms for small payloads, max allowed CPU budget per request 0.5ms equivalent.
- Reliability / safety: default is fail-open for low-severity violations; fail-closed only for explicit high-risk rules (PII-policy, schema-critical).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests covering strict/permissive/fuzzy paths and edge cases (malformed JSON, huge arrays, nested schema drift).
- Synthetic throughput test: sustain 2000 rps with median added latency <2ms on a standard ingestion node (test harness attached).
- Canary rollout: 1% of tenant traffic for 48 hours with detailed dashboards and auto-scaling enabled.
- Console UI: add an operations view that surfaces recent quarantine samples and a quick link to create a support-ticket/backfill job.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy Arbiter in passive mode (emit decisions only) to staging; validate telemetry and false-positive rate with historical replay.
2) Deploy to production as passive (0% action) for 72h; monitor data quality dashboards, product-reported anomalies, and error rates.
3) Enable policy-driven coercions for internal tenants only (10% sample) for 48h.
4) Expand to all tenants with canary + gradual ramp to 100% in 6 steps.

Security & privacy: Arbiter will strip any free-text heuristics outputs from logs for PII-sensitive fields and rely on KMS-encrypted storage for sampled payloads retained for debugging. Security review will be required for the quarantine retention policy.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Decision telemetry emitted to metrics pipeline (datadog/grafana).
- Alert if 5xx rate increases >0.2% relative to baseline post-rollout.
- Monitor false-accept rate against a labeled evaluation set; threshold for rollback is 0.3% increase in false-accepts causing customer-facing anomalies.

Operational playbooks and followups:
- Quarantine consumer: small worker to surface samples to SRE/Support (manual triage) and optionally trigger backfill jobs.
- Post-deploy retrospective and automated regression test added to CI (replay of last 7 days of sampled traffic).
